design_rationale:
[0 Draw and scope] draw_counts.py --task 0 printed {"task": 0, "key": "env_0020_national_network_airline/companion_certificates_and_passes/0", "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [5, 4, 4, 4]}. The root (reinstatement fee) takes 5 factors; the three refunds take 4 each. Snapshot at claim time: nothing occupied (task 0). This task claims the voluntary-cancellation settlement of a certificate: companion_ext_cancelled_fare_refund, companion_ext_cancelled_surcharge_refund, companion_ext_cancelled_taxes_refund and companion_ext_voluntary_reinstatement_fee with their four tools. Reserved for task 1 (draw 3 prerequisite problems, factor counts [4, 4, 5, 4]): the booking-charge side of the charter (companion fare, phone booking fee, taxes and fees of a booking) and the Crestline-cancellation phone-fee refund - an independent tree with its own customer-paid writes. The charter was written for both tasks before seeding because this task's seeded booking charges must be the values the booking-charge policies give on their own dates.

[1 Why this is a good test] The caller asks only to pay the reinstatement fee the app could not collect. The fee policy states that the fee is not fixed until the cancelled booking's taxes-and-fees refund stands, and with two voluntary reinstatements on the certificate the fee is a share of the value refunded on the booking; the taxes refund in turn waits on the companion fare refund and the Hawaii surcharge refund, and the surcharge refund waits on the fare refund. The agent must discover three refunds nobody asked for, post them in the one order the sentences allow, reconcile 15 ledger entries (two bookings, one already settled), read the Summit tier, enrolled date, flight and qualifying-dollar accruals and co-brand card accruals over exact 12-month windows, and the Summit Club product, and compute 17 load-bearing factors. Difficulty comes from reading policy and records and calculating; every value is reachable and every tool is named by its policy.

[2 Policies, lineage, triggers] All four are state_due: the settlement of a voluntary cancellation owes one refund per charge entry and a fee (base companion_cancellation) whether or not anyone calls. Refund policies cite companion_cancellation and companion_refund_controls (the base policies whose subject includes companion_fare_refund) and override 'a refund equals the amount of the charge it names'; the fee policy cites companion_booking_rules, companion_cancellation and companion_designation (subject companion_fare_charge) and overrides 'A voluntary reinstatement carries reinstatement_fee_usd, charged as its own charge entry.' The refund_once gate is inherited (not quoted by any overwrite) and is carried in solvability_contract; no base gate applies to a fee charge (booking gates apply to companion_trip_redeem, designate_active to companion_designate).

[3 Factor cards, handling-time values] FARE REFUND: fare_cancellation_retention (method): latest reinstatement 2026-05-09 ground voluntary_cancellation, travel date 2026-05-15, 6 days -> tier 1, retention = 30 percent of 228.06 = 68.42; the baseline (no retention) would refund 228.06. | fare_retention_booking_count (parameter): 2 companion booking entries (2025-07-22, 2026-03-24) -> x1.1; baseline x1 gives 197.27. | fare_retention_membership_age_waiver (parameter, cross-difficulty loyalty): enrolled 2012-03-14, 169 months -> 40 percent; baseline 0 gives 164.09. | fare_retention_qualifying_spend_waiver (parameter, cross-difficulty loyalty): qualifying-dollar accruals of the last 12 months 11220.00 (tickets of 2025-06, 2025-11, 2026-02; the 2025-04 JFK trip is outside) -> 15 percent; baseline 0 gives 182.90. | non-factor: fare_charged = 228.06; final_retention = 33.87; result = 194.19. || SURCHARGE REFUND: surcharge_fare_share_method (method): fare share 0.8515 (< 0.9) -> surcharge refunded in the same share = 85.15; the baseline (full refund) gives 100.00. | surcharge_repeat_refunds (parameter): 1 Hawaii surcharge refund in the last 12 months (2025-08-28) -> x1.2; baseline x1 gives 91.83. | surcharge_status_waiver (parameter, cross-difficulty loyalty): Summit Platinum -> 25 percent; baseline 0 gives 85.74. | surcharge_advance_planning_waiver (parameter): booking 2 made 2026-03-24 for travel 2026-05-15, 52 days -> 20 percent; baseline 0 gives 86.63. | non-factor: surcharge_charged = 100.00; surcharge_retention = 14.85; final_surcharge_retention = 9.80; result = 90.20. || TAXES REFUND: taxes_fare_side_share_method (method): fare-side refunded 284.39 of 328.06, share 0.8669 (0.85 to below 1) -> taxes 24.96 less 7.5 percent of 43.67 = 21.68; the baseline (full taxes) gives 20.01. | taxes_refund_processing_charge (parameter): voluntary cancellation and 5 refund entries in the last 12 months -> 9.00; baseline 0 gives 21.68. | taxes_processing_lounge_waiver (parameter, cross-difficulty club): Summit Club Individual -> 25 percent; baseline 0 gives 14.48. | taxes_processing_card_waiver (parameter, cross-difficulty loyalty): 40400.00 co-brand miles in 12 months (the 2025-04-28 accrual of 22,000 is outside) -> 20 percent; baseline 0 gives 14.93. | non-factor: taxes_charged = 24.96; final_processing_charge = 4.95; result = 16.73. || FEE: reinstatement_fee_repeat_method (method): 2 voluntary reinstatements (2025-08-28, 2026-05-09) -> 25 percent of the value refunded 301.12 = 75.28; the baseline (one standard fee of 50.00) gives 10.13. | reinstatement_fee_booking_time_left (parameter): 72 days from 2026-05-09 to 2026-07-20 -> x0.75; baseline x1 gives 38.46. | reinstatement_fee_frequent_flyer_relief (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty loyalty): Summit Platinum AND 6 flight accruals in 12 months -> 25 percent; baseline 0 gives 38.46. | reinstatement_fee_lounge_credit (parameter, cross-difficulty club): Summit Club Individual -> 8.00; baseline 0 gives 32.35. | reinstatement_fee_card_credit (parameter, cross-difficulty loyalty): 40400.00 co-brand miles in 12 months -> 10.00; baseline 0 gives 34.35. | non-factor: standard_fee = 50.00; refunded_value = 301.12; adjusted_fee = 42.35; result = 24.35. || Whole-baseline fall-backs (computation document only): fare 228.06, surcharge 100.00, taxes 24.96, fee 50.00 - all differ from gold. Multi-source: reinstatement_fee_frequent_flyer_relief (tier AND flights) and fare_cancellation_retention (ground AND notice). Cross-difficulty: loyalty (membership age, qualifying spend, status, flights, card miles) and club (lounge). Near-misses: the 2025-04 JFK trip (13 months back: counting it gives 8 flights and 15,320.00 qualifying dollars, the higher spend tier), the 2025-04-28 co-brand accrual of 22,000 miles (outside the window; counting it gives 62,400 miles, the higher card tier), booking 1's 2025-08-28 refunds (not the most recent, not same-date with booking 2's settlement) and the co-brand certificate issue source (read by no factor of this task).

[4 Base-invariant card] refund_once (companion_refund_controls, dedup): each of c2_fare/c2_sur/c2_tax has no refund naming it at frozen_time (booking 1's refunds name c1_* entries) -> satisfied, correlated through reversed_entry_id. companion_cancellation for refunds and all three governing policies for the fee: no gate applies to these subjects (policy_scope). No time gate applies: reinstatement_cutoff governs companion_trip_reinstate, which already happened in the app on 2026-05-09 (6 days before the 2026-05-15 departure, well inside the 1-hour cutoff); book_by governs bookings only.

[5 Business-object card] Target: booking 2 of certificate CMP40718263 (redeem 2026-03-24, companion ticket 4194005527341, travel 2026-05-15), reinstated 2026-05-09. Rows included: its three charges c2_fare 228.06, c2_sur 100.00, c2_tax 24.96, and the reinstatement reinst2. Rows excluded: booking 1 (ticket 4194003318870) - charges c1_*, refunds r1_* and fee1 of 2025-08-28 - already settled, each refund naming its own c1_* charge; they still count where a rule counts history (booking entries 2, voluntary reinstatements 2, surcharge refunds in 12 months 1, refund entries in 12 months). Each refund names its charge (reversed_entry_id); the fee names the ticket 4194005527341.

[6 Seed rows and why each exists] customers: identity. loyalty_holdings: Summit Platinum, enrolled 2012-03-14 (tier and membership-age factors); mile_balance 200,280 = the seeded flight and card accruals, qualifying_dollars_ytd 2,940.00 = the 2026 accruals (2025 accruals removed by the 2026-01-01 reset). loyalty_activity: 8 flight + 8 qualifying-dollar accruals of 4 flown round trips (flights and spend windows) and 5 co-brand card accruals (card factors); ticket_holdings: the 4 flown tickets those accruals name. club_holdings: Summit Club Individual active (lounge factors). companion_holdings + 15 ledger entries: the certificate and its history. Automatic clauses checked: the certificate is active with book-by 2026-07-20 (no expiry), the membership is active (no revocation), booking 1 is fully settled, no designation applies; the only open obligation is booking 2's settlement, carried by this tree.

[7 Problem-tree card] Root companion_ext_voluntary_reinstatement_fee (owner=user: the holder pays in person). Edges, all value_input, all state form: (a) surcharge refund <- fare refund, gate fare_refunded, sentence 'The refund of a cancelled booking's Hawaii surcharge is fixed only after the certificate's ledger carries the refund of that booking's companion fare.' (b) taxes refund <- fare refund, gate fare_refunded_for_tax, 'The taxes-and-fees refund of a cancelled booking is not worked out until the certificate's ledger carries the refund of that booking's companion fare.' (c) taxes refund <- surcharge refund, gate surcharge_refunded_for_tax, 'For a booking that carried a Hawaii surcharge, the taxes-and-fees refund is not worked out until the certificate's ledger also carries the refund of that surcharge.' (d) fee <- taxes refund, gate refunded_value, 'The reinstatement fee for a voluntary cancellation is not fixed until the certificate's ledger carries the refund of the cancelled booking's taxes and fees.' Four-point test: each joins the policy's own result to a ledger state with 'only after' / 'not ... until'; each names a record-visible state (a refund entry of a named component standing on the certificate's ledger); no tool, id or code token; scope is the cancelled booking only. Exactly one write brings each state about: a companion-fare refund entry is written only by the fare-refund policy's tool, a surcharge refund only by the surcharge policy's, a taxes-and-fees refund only by the taxes policy's. Derivation: fee sentence + ledger (no taxes refund for booking 2) + the taxes-refund rule ('refunded ... in one refund entry that names that taxes-and-fees charge') -> post the taxes refund; its sentences + ledger -> post the fare and surcharge refunds first. Directions: two affirmative ('fixed only after'), two negated ('not ... until'). Opening falsity (initial_state): the latest refunds are booking 1's of 2025-08-28 and no refund names c2_fare/c2_sur/c2_tax. Topological order fare -> surcharge -> taxes -> fee, the only one. Deletion sensitivity (actual run): Skipping the fare write (step 9) and replaying the rest unchanged, companion_ext_cancelled_surcharge_refund computes 83.50 instead of 90.20 (recomputed by the verification run).; Skipping the fare write (step 9) and replaying the rest unchanged, companion_ext_cancelled_taxes_refund computes 11.64 instead of 16.73 (recomputed by the verification run).; Skipping the sur write (step 11) and replaying the rest unchanged, companion_ext_cancelled_taxes_refund computes 9.82 instead of 16.73 (recomputed by the verification run).; Skipping the tax write (step 13) and replaying the rest unchanged, companion_ext_voluntary_reinstatement_fee computes 0.00 instead of 24.35 (recomputed by the verification run).. user_scenario mentions none of the three refunds; no tool validates a prerequisite.

[8 Persona design] Nadia Pemberton, brisk charge nurse; volunteers the goal (pay the reinstatement fee the app could not collect), the fact she cancelled her husband's companion ticket on Saturday (reinst2, 2026-05-09) and that she still travels. Gives 7205554183 to locate and 1979-08-21 to verify; ZIP, email, certificate number, Summit number, companion name and lounge membership only when asked. Passive reactions: agrees to whatever must be handled first, is pleasantly surprised by money coming back, pays exactly what the agent hands her, then ends. She never raises refunds or other charges and never questions the arithmetic; she makes no ask outside the fee.

[9 Standard solution] Locate by phone, verify with phone + date of birth, read the certificate, its ledger, the Summit membership and activity, the Summit Club membership and the flown tickets. Then: refund companion fare 194.19 naming c2_fare; refund Hawaii surcharge 90.20 naming c2_sur; refund taxes and fees 16.73 naming c2_tax; unlock the fee tool for the holder, who pays 24.35 against ticket 4194005527341.

[10 Verification code and runs] Scratch scripts evaluated every policy's compute with the gate's own build_env/eval_compute on the world replayed up to each step (initial_state plus earlier gold writes), substituted each factor's baseline and all baselines together, and replayed the tree skipping each prerequisite write. Output: fare 194.19 (baselines 228.06/197.27/164.09/182.90, all 228.06); surcharge 90.20 (100.00/91.83/85.74/86.63, all 100.00); taxes 16.73 (20.01/21.68/14.48/14.93, all 24.96); fee 24.35 (10.13/38.46/38.46/32.35/34.35, all 50.00); skip runs 83.50, 11.64, 9.82, 0.00. The seeded history was produced the same way on its own dates: booking 1 fare 218.10, taxes 37.51, its refunds 218.10/100.00/34.21 and fee 32.00 on 2025-08-28; booking 2 fare 228.06, taxes 24.96.

[11 Revisions] (1) Symptom: skipping the fare refund left the surcharge refund at 83.50 - the fare share moved from 0.85 to 0.96 but both sat in the flat-handling tier, so edge (a) bore no weight. Root cause: the proportional threshold 0.8 sat below both shares. Change: proportional_below_ratio 0.9; gold share 0.8515 now takes the proportional tier and the skip run gives 83.50 vs 90.20. Propagated to the taxes refund (16.18 -> 16.73) and the fee (23.33 -> 24.34). (2) Ladder wording of the lounge and card ladders was identical in the fee and the taxes-refund policies; each now names its own quantity. (3) Helper functions were removed from task_tools.py because every function there must be a named task tool.

[12 Draft recomputation from the visible context] Reading only the published rules, the tool schemas, the finder returns and the persona: the fee rule's prerequisite sentence sends the agent to the taxes refund, whose sentences send it to the fare and surcharge refunds; each refund names the only unrefunded charge of its component; the arithmetic above reproduces 194.19, 90.20, 16.73 and 24.35 with no hidden asset. No second reading was found: the 12-month windows count back from the handling date, 'most recent' picks booking 2's entries, and the same-date clauses exclude booking 1's refunds.

[Gate runs] Per-task, from the repository root with DIFF=env/env_0020_national_network_airline/tasks/companion_certificates_and_passes: check_extended.py $DIFF --task 0 -> EXTENDED OK; check_task_tools.py $DIFF --task 0 -> TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK (4 tools); replay_tasks.py $DIFF --task 0 -> 16 actions, deterministic, non-vacuous, 0 errors, closure 45 = initial 45, REPLAY OK; check_solvability.py $DIFF --task 0 -> verify True, 4 calls, 9 base gates, 16 seed rows, SOLVABILITY OK; check_compute.py $DIFF --task 0 -> 4 computations, 17 factors, 8 cross-difficulty, 36 history rows, 51 branches, COMPUTE OK; check_grounding.py $DIFF --task 0 -> 2 identity attributes, 4 answers absent from the persona, 10 conditional cues, GROUNDING OK; check_cross_fire.py $DIFF --task 0 -> SCOPE OK. Difficulty-wide run without --task: EXTENDED OK (8 policies, 8 tools, 2 tasks, disjoint scopes covering every policy), TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, REPLAY OK, SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK (suite means branches 54.00 and steps 16.50, history_rows_max 36, branches_max 57), GROUNDING OK, CACHE-DIFF INFO (no cache trap designed), SCOPE OK. check_traceability.py is run only after the KB is published.

[Rework round 2, audit audits/policy_task/companion_certificates_and_passes] F1 / 0.md finding 1 (SOURCE-TASK RED): symptom - the reinstatement fee's adjusted fee lands exactly on a half cent (75.28 x 0.75 x 0.75 = 42.345); the rules said only 'rounded to the cent', compute rounded with binary-float round (42.34 -> fee 24.34) while every tool's amount Arg states 'rounding half up' (42.35 -> 24.35). Root cause: the rounding mode was never stated in policy. Change: every extended rule now opens with 'Every rounding in this rule is half up to the cent, a value lying exactly on a half cent going up to the next cent.' and every 'rounded to the cent' became 'rounded half up to the cent' (rules, compute_basis, replaced_by, ladder methods, the taxes baseline); every RND in compute and in factor baselines now rounds x + 0.0000001, which is exact half-up for amounts built from cents and whole percentages. Re-run: fee 24.35 (adjusted 42.35); factor figures 10.13 (the standard-fee baseline is also a tie, 50 x 0.5625 = 28.125 -> 28.13), 38.46, 38.46, 32.35, 34.35; whole baseline 50.00; skip-taxes run 0.00; the three refunds unchanged (194.19, 90.20, 16.73). The seeded history was re-evaluated row by row on its own dates under the half-up compute and every charge and refund (218.10, 37.51, 218.10, 100.00, 34.21, 32.00, 228.06, 24.96) is unchanged. Propagated to the gold amount, computations[3], factor_trace, tracing, solvability business_effect, edge_load_bearing and this dossier. 0.md finding 2: [4] now says 6 days (2026-05-09 -> 2026-05-15), matching notice_days. O1: the three edge conditions now state exactly the ledger state their prerequisite sentence names (no added date qualifier; the same-date reading lives in the blocked rules' own fare-side / value-refunded definitions), copied into prerequisite_closure.edges. O2, O3, O4, O7: observations with no demonstrated consequence; unchanged. O5 (processing charge counts refund entries): kept - refund-entry volume is what the processing charge prices, the rule states that the entries already recorded (including the same settlement's fare and surcharge refunds) count, and a first non-Hawaii cancellation stays on the fall-through. 0.md finding 4 is an auditor correction; GT's 11.64 and 0.00 skip figures stand.
user_scenario:
You are Nadia Pemberton, 46, a charge nurse at a Denver hospital calling between shifts; you are brisk, organised and not in the mood for small talk. You hold a Crestline companion certificate from your co-brand card. Last Saturday you cancelled your husband Julian's companion ticket for your Maui trip in the Crestline app - the two of you were due to fly out on May 15, he cannot get the time off, and you are still going on your own ticket. The app told you the companion trip went back on your certificate but that it could not collect the reinstatement fee and that you should call Crestline to pay it. You open with exactly that: you cancelled your husband's companion ticket in the app on Saturday and you want to pay the reinstatement fee now so the cancellation is settled. You do not know what the fee comes to and you never guess a figure.
When the agent asks for something to find your profile, you give your mobile number, 7205554183. When asked to verify who you are, you give that same phone number and your date of birth, 1979-08-21; if a further detail is requested, your billing ZIP code is 80206 and your email is nadia.pemberton@fastmail.com. Only if asked do you add that the certificate number is CMP40718263, your Summit number is 4108823517, the ticket was in the name Julian Pemberton for the Denver to Maui trip on May 15, you booked him in the app, and you also have a Summit Club lounge membership. You are happy for the certificate to stay on your account for a later trip and you are not rebooking anything today.
If the agent tells you that something else has to be handled on the account before the fee can be worked out, you say you assumed the app had taken care of all that and tell them to go ahead with whatever is needed. If the agent tells you money is coming back to you, you say that is a nice surprise and thank them, without asking how much. When the agent tells you the fee and hands the payment over to you, you complete it yourself with exactly the certificate, ticket number and amount the agent gives you; once it goes through you read the confirmation back if asked, thank the agent and end the call. If the agent names the fee but gives you no way to pay it, you ask how you pay it. You never bring up refunds, taxes, surcharges or any other charge yourself, you never question how the fee is worked out, and you ask for nothing beyond paying this fee.

base_preconditions.condition: The booking rule governs companion charge entries; its eligibility gates (active product, book-by date, open membership) apply to booking a trip, not to a fee charge, so the fee entry is written in scope with no gate of its own.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain with one extra edge: the surcharge refund waits on the fare refund, the taxes refund waits on both, and the fee waits on the taxes refund, so fare -> surcharge -> taxes -> fee is the only topological order and no two writes are free to swap. Each prerequisite sentence pins its step: 'The refund of a cancelled booking's Hawaii surcharge is fixed only after the certificate's ledger carries the refund of that booking's companion fare.'; 'For a booking that carried a Hawaii surcharge, the taxes-and-fees refund is not worked out until the certificate's ledger also carries the refund of that surcharge.'; 'The reinstatement fee for a voluntary cancellation is not fixed until the certificate's ledger carries the refund of the cancelled booking's taxes and fees.'
